title: A writ petition under Art 32 (Supreme Court) or Art 226 (High Court) seeks enforcement of Fundamental Rights (and under Art 226, other legal rights)

content.overview: A writ petition under Art 32 (Supreme Court) or Art 226 (High Court) seeks enforcement of Fundamental Rights (and under Art 226, other legal rights). Exam awareness focuses on parties, grounds, prayer, and the five writs — not a full drafting course.
content.short: A writ petition under Art 32 (Supreme Court) or Art 226 (High Court) seeks enforcement of Fundamental Rights (and under Art 226, other legal rights). Exam awareness focuses on parties, grounds, prayer, and the five writs — not a full drafting course.
content.detailed:
Typical skeleton (exam / drafting awareness)

1. Cause title
   • Court name (Supreme Court of India / High Court of …)
   • Writ Petition (Civil/Criminal) No. … of …
   • Petitioner(s) vs Respondent(s)

2. Memo of parties
   • Full names, addresses, capacity

3. Synopsis / list of dates (often required in practice)

4. Facts
   • Chronological narrative of relevant facts
   • How the petitioner is aggrieved

5. Grounds
   • Legal grounds (violation of FR / legal right)
   • Cite articles/sections and key cases where relevant

6. Prayer
   • Specific writ(s) sought: habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, quo warranto
   • Interim relief if any
   • Costs

7. Affidavit / verification

Five writs (quick recall)
• Habeas corpus — produce the person; challenge illegal detention
• Mandamus — command a public authority to perform a duty
• Prohibition — stop a lower court/tribunal from exceeding jurisdiction
• Certiorari — quash an order of a lower court/tribunal
• Quo warranto — challenge authority to hold a public office

Art 32 vs Art 226
• Art 32 — Fundamental Right; only FR enforcement; SC
• Art 226 — wider (FR + other legal rights); HC; discretionary

Exam tip: AIBE rarely asks full drafting; it tests which writ fits a fact pattern and Art 32/226 differences.

cases.name: Romesh Thappar v. State of Madras
cases.holding: Art 32 is a fundamental right; SC is the protector of FRs.
cases.relevance: Character of Art 32 as a guaranteed remedy.

cases.name: L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India
cases.holding: Power of judicial review under Arts 32 and 226 is part of the basic structure.
cases.relevance: Writ jurisdiction cannot be ousted in substance.

examTips: Match the fact pattern to the correct writ (especially habeas corpus vs mandamus).
Art 32 = FR only + SC; Art 226 = wider + HC.
Prayer must specify the writ and the exact relief.
AIBE focuses on concept and correct writ, not long drafting.
